questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: If i = √-1, find the value of i^15.
questions.exp: i cycles every 4: i,−1,−i,1. 15=4×3+3. i^15=i³=−i.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: Find the sum of roots of the equation 3x² - 9x + 6 = 0.
questions.exp: Sum of roots = -b/a = -(-9)/3 = 3.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: If cos θ = 4/5, find sin θ (θ in first quadrant).
questions.exp: cos=4/5 → adjacent=4, hypotenuse=5, opposite=3 (3-4-5 triplet). sin=3/5.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: Evaluate: lim(x→0) (sin 3x)/x
questions.exp: lim(x→0) sin(kx)/x = k. Here k=3, so the limit is 3.

questions.exp: ∫4x dx=2x². ∫3 dx=3x. Total=2x²+3x+C.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Choose the correct sentence:
questions.exp: Third person singular subject 'He' requires 'doesn't' + base verb form: 'He doesn't know the answer'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Synonym of TENACIOUS:
questions.exp: Tenacious means tending to keep a firm hold; persistent and determined.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Fill in the blank: He has been working here ___ 2018.
questions.exp: 'Since' is used with a specific starting point in time. 'For' would be used with a duration like 'for 6 years'.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The SI unit of electric resistance is:
questions.exp: The SI unit of electric resistance is Ohm (Ω), as defined by Ohm's Law: V=IR.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A body of mass 5kg accelerates at 4 m/s². Find the force applied.
questions.exp: F=ma=5×4=20 Newtons.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The escape velocity from Earth's surface is approximately:
questions.exp: Escape velocity from Earth's surface is approximately 11.2 km/s, the minimum speed needed to break free from Earth's gravity.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of these is a noble gas?
questions.exp: Argon is a noble gas (Group 18), characterized by complete outer electron shells and low reactivity.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The pH value of a neutral solution at 25°C is:
questions.exp: A neutral solution has a pH value of 7 at 25°C, as in pure water.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The First Battle of Panipat (1526) was fought between Babur and:
questions.exp: The First Battle of Panipat (1526) was fought between Babur and Ibrahim Lodi, the last Delhi Sultanate ruler, establishing Mughal rule in India.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: Who was the founder of the Indian National Army (INA)?
opts: Both Rash Behari Bose and Mohan Singh initially
questions.exp: INA was initially organized by Captain Mohan Singh in 1942 and Rash Behari Bose, before Subhash Chandra Bose reorganized and led it in 1943.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which is the largest continent by area?
questions.exp: Asia is the largest continent by both area and population.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Tropic of Cancer passes through which of these Indian states?
questions.exp: The Tropic of Cancer passes through Gujarat among others, but not through Punjab, Haryana, or Himachal Pradesh.

questions.subject: Current
questions.q: Chandrayaan-3's lander module successfully landed on the Moon in which year?
questions.exp: Chandrayaan-3 successfully landed near the Moon's south pole on 23 August 2023.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: The National Defence Academy (NDA) is located in which city?
questions.exp: The National Defence Academy is located at Khadakwasla, near Pune, Maharashtra.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: India's Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) post was created in which year?
questions.exp: The post of Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) was created in 2019, with General Bipin Rawat being the first to hold the position.

questions.q: If the discriminant of a quadratic equation is zero, the roots are:
questions.exp: When discriminant (b²-4ac)=0, the quadratic equation has real and equal roots.

questions.q: Find the derivative of y = e^(2x) with respect to x.
questions.exp: Using chain rule: dy/dx = 2e^(2x).

questions.q: If a x b (cross product) = 0 for two non-zero vectors, the vectors are:
questions.exp: When the cross product of two non-zero vectors is zero, the vectors are parallel (sin θ = 0, so θ = 0° or 180°).

questions.exp: log₁₀(x)=2 means 10²=x, so x=100.

questions.q: Find the area of triangle with vertices (0,0), (5,0), and (0,4).
questions.exp: With base along x-axis (5) and height along y-axis (4): Area=½×5×4=10.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Choose the correct sentence:
opts: She is one of the best student in the class
She is one of the best students in the class
She are one of the best students
She is one best student in class
questions.exp: 'One of the' is followed by a plural noun: 'one of the best students'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Antonym of CANDID:
questions.exp: Candid means truthful and straightforward. Antonym = Deceptive (misleading or dishonest).

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Fill in the blank: Neither the captain nor the players ___ satisfied with the result.
questions.exp: With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject. 'Players' (plural) is nearer, so 'were' is correct.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which law states that every action has an equal and opposite reaction?
questions.exp: Newton's Third Law states that for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The speed of sound in air at room temperature is approximately:
questions.exp: The speed of sound in air at approximately 20-25°C is about 343 m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which type of mirror is used in vehicle headlights to produce a parallel beam of light?
questions.exp: Concave mirrors are used in vehicle headlights because they can produce a parallel beam of light when the source is placed at the focus.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which gas is commonly known as 'laughing gas'?
questions.exp: Nitrous oxide (N2O) is commonly known as 'laughing gas' and is used as a mild anesthetic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Rusting of iron is an example of which type of reaction?
questions.exp: Rusting of iron is an oxidation reaction, where iron reacts with oxygen and moisture to form iron oxide.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The 'Doctrine of Lapse' policy was associated with which Governor-General?
questions.exp: Lord Dalhousie introduced the Doctrine of Lapse, leading to the annexation of several princely states without a male heir.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: Operation Vijay (1999) is associated with which conflict?
questions.exp: Operation Vijay was India's military operation during the Kargil War (1999) to recapture positions held by Pakistani infiltrators.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The longest river in the world is:
questions.exp: The Nile River in Africa is traditionally considered the longest river in the world, at approximately 6,650 km.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which Indian state has the highest forest cover (by percentage of geographical area)?
questions.exp: Mizoram has the highest forest cover by percentage of its geographical area among Indian states.

questions.subject: Current
questions.q: INS Vikrant, India's indigenous aircraft carrier, was commissioned in which year?
questions.exp: INS Vikrant, India's first indigenously built aircraft carrier, was commissioned in September 2022.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: AFCAT stands for:
questions.exp: AFCAT stands for Air Force Common Admission Test, used for recruiting officers into the Indian Air Force.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: Which Indian missile system is known as a Multiple Independently targetable Re-entry Vehicle (MIRV) capable missile?
questions.exp: Agni-5 is India's long-range ballistic missile equipped with MIRV technology, successfully tested with this capability.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: If sin A = cos A, find the value of A (0°<A<90°).
questions.exp: sin A = cos A implies tan A = 1, so A = 45°.

questions.q: Find the value of: ∫₀^1 x² dx
questions.exp: ∫x²dx=x³/3. Evaluating from 0 to 1: (1³/3)-(0³/3)=1/3.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: How many ways can 4 different books be arranged on a shelf?
questions.exp: Number of arrangements = 4! = 4×3×2×1 = 24.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: If a die is thrown once, find the probability of getting a number greater than 4.
questions.exp: Numbers greater than 4 on a die: 5,6 (2 outcomes). P=2/6=1/3.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: If a matrix A is of order 2×3 and matrix B is of order 3×2, what is the order of matrix AB?
questions.exp: For matrix multiplication, if A is m×n and B is n×p, AB is m×p. Here 2×3 multiplied by 3×2 gives 2×2.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: Find the mean of the numbers 4, 8, 12, 16, 20.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.q: If the angle of elevation of the sun changes from 30° to 60°, the length of the shadow of a tower decreases by 50m. Find the height of the tower.
questions.exp: Using tan30°=h/x and tan60°=h/(x-50): h=x/√3 and h=√3(x-50). Solving gives h=25√3 m.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Choose the correct sentence:
opts: He is taller than I am
He is more tall than me
He is much taller from me
questions.exp: In formal comparative constructions, 'than I am' (subject form) is grammatically preferred, though 'than me' is colloquially common.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Synonym of RELUCTANT:
questions.exp: Reluctant means unwilling or disinclined to do something.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Fill in the blank: I would have helped you if I ___ known earlier.
questions.exp: In third conditional sentences (past unreal), 'had' + past participle is used in the if-clause: 'if I had known'.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The unit of power in the SI system is:
questions.exp: The SI unit of power is the Watt (W), defined as one Joule per second.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which phenomenon explains why the sky appears blue?
questions.exp: The sky appears blue due to Rayleigh scattering, where shorter wavelengths (blue) are scattered more than longer wavelengths by atmospheric particles.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A body is thrown vertically upward with velocity 20 m/s. Find the maximum height reached (g=10 m/s²).
questions.exp: Using v²=u²-2gh, at max height v=0: 0=400-2×10×h. h=400/20=20m.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The chemical formula of baking soda is:
questions.exp: Baking soda is Sodium Bicarbonate, with chemical formula NaHCO3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which element has the chemical symbol 'Au'?
questions.exp: 'Au' is the chemical symbol for Gold, derived from the Latin word 'Aurum'.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: The Treaty of Sugauli (1816) was signed between the British and:
questions.exp: The Treaty of Sugauli (1816) was signed between the British East India Company and the Kingdom of Nepal, ending the Anglo-Nepalese War.

questions.subject: History
questions.q: Who gave the famous slogan 'Jai Hind'?
questions.exp: Subhash Chandra Bose popularized the slogan 'Jai Hind' as a salutation for the Indian National Army (INA).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which is the deepest point in the world's oceans?
questions.exp: The Mariana Trench in the Pacific Ocean is the deepest known point in the world's oceans, reaching depths of about 11,000m.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The 'Ring of Fire' is associated with which natural phenomenon?
questions.exp: The 'Ring of Fire' is a region around the Pacific Ocean known for frequent volcanic eruptions and earthquakes due to tectonic plate boundaries.

questions.subject: Current
questions.q: India's Gaganyaan mission aims to send astronauts to:
questions.exp: Gaganyaan is India's first human spaceflight mission, aiming to send astronauts to Low Earth Orbit.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: The Indian Navy's Agniveer scheme covers which entry categories?
questions.exp: The Indian Navy's Agniveer scheme covers Senior Secondary Recruits (SSR) and Matric Recruits (MR) for sailor-level entries.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: Operation Shakti, India's nuclear tests, was conducted in which year?
questions.exp: Operation Shakti, India's series of five nuclear tests, was conducted at Pokhran in May 1998.
